title: BriDGE — Development Handoff
text: R package implementing BriDGE protocol mechanistic analysis RCT data: Causal discovery RCT data experimental constraints — treatment→mediator edges whitelisted, edges treatment blacklisted — via bnlearn (MMHC default; HC PC-stable also supported). Continuous variables discretized (Hmisc::cut2, default 5 bins) mutual-information tests. Mediation analysis GAMs (mgcv) capture nonlinear mediator–outcome relationships; estimates natural direct effect, per-mediator indirect effects, total effect via counterfactual prediction, bootstrap CIs. Sensitivity analysis Gaussian perturbation mediators/outcome, re-running mediation. Comparison & visualization: researcher-DAG vs discovered-DAG edge comparison, group-mean comparison, bootstrap-distribution effect-size plots (ggplot2).

title: Getting started with BriDGE
text: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) tell whether intervention works. rarely designed tell works — mediators carry effect, whether relationships nonlinear, whether theoretical causal model actually consistent data. BriDGE implements protocol described companion paper (Veltri & Banerjee, press, Behavior Research Methods), combining: researcher’s DAG — theoretical causal model experiment. Causal discovery — structure learning constrained experimental design facts (randomized treatment can affect variables, nothing can cause treatment). GAM-based mediation analysis — direct indirect effects estimated flexible smooth functions instead rigid linear terms. Bootstrap inference sensitivity checks — effects come uncertainty robustness information. vignette walks full workflow synthetic data ground truth known.
code: library(BriDGE)

title: Getting started with BriDGE
text: bridge_generate_data() generates synthetic two-arm RCT binary treatment, two mediators, continuous outcome. data-generating process deliberately includes nonlinearities (quadratic mediator effect, mediator–mediator interaction, treatment--mediator interactions), mirroring simulation study paper. data need: two-level treatment factor (first factor level taken control, second treated), numeric mediators, numeric outcome, missing values analysis variables:

what: 2. Causal discovery: does the data agree with your DAG?
title: Getting started with BriDGE
text: bridge_discover() learns DAG data enforcing know design: edges treatment mediator whitelisted (randomization guarantees treatment upstream), edge treatment blacklisted. row edge; Researcher marks edges assumed DAG (treatment mediator outcome, mediator outcome), Discovered marks edges algorithm found. Read disagreements hypotheses examine, verdicts: edge algorithm finds mediators, example, suggests parallel-mediator theory may miss mediator--mediator pathway. Discovery discretized data also sensitive binning choices, treat low-stability edges caution (see paper’s discussion arc-strength stability). can plot structures:
code: discovery <- bridge_discover(   data      = data,   treatment = "treatment",   mediators = c("mediator_1", "mediator_2"),   outcome   = "outcome",   method    = "mmhc"   # also: "hc", "pc" )  discovery$comparison #>         From         To Researcher Discovered #> 1 mediator_1    outcome       TRUE       TRUE #> 2 mediator_2    outcome       TRUE      FALSE #> 3  treatment mediator_1       TRUE       TRUE #> 4  treatment mediator_2       TRUE       TRUE #> 5  treatment    outcome       TRUE       TRUE plot(discovery$researcher_dag)     # your theory plot(discovery$discovered_igraph)  # what the data suggests

title: Getting started with BriDGE
text: bridge_mediate() decomposes treatment effect using counterfactual prediction outcome GAM smooth terms mediator: direct_effect — natural direct effect: treatment’s effect outcome holding mediators control-condition values. nie_<mediator> — indirect effect mediator: outcome change produced shifting mediator (one) control treated value. total_effect — treatment’s overall effect mediators responding. Confidence intervals come bootstrap resampling. use small number bootstraps keep vignette fast — use 500–2000 real analyses. interval excludes zero indicates reliable effect 95% level. outcome model uses smooth terms, estimates remain valid mediator–outcome relationships curved — exactly situation classic linear mediation (e.g., product--coefficients) can biased. Setting nonlinear = FALSE re-runs everything linear models, useful comparison: two disagree, nonlinearity matters.
code: mediation <- bridge_mediate(   data         = data,   treatment    = "treatment",   mediators    = c("mediator_1", "mediator_2"),   outcome      = "outcome",   n_bootstraps = 50,      # use >= 500 in practice   nonlinear    = TRUE,    # GAM smooths for mediator-outcome links   parallel     = FALSE,   # TRUE recommended on your machine   seed         = 42 )  for (effect in names(mediation$summaries)) {   s <- mediation$summaries[[effect]]   cat(sprintf("%-16s % .3f  [% .3f, % .3f]\n",               effect, s$mean, s$ci_lower, s$ci_upper)) } #> direct_effect     2.491  [ 2.288,  2.723] #> total_effect      6.023  [ 5.538,  6.528] #> nie_mediator_1    2.276  [ 1.874,  2.674] #> nie_mediator_2    1.257  [ 0.922,  1.591]

title: Getting started with BriDGE
text: bridge_sensitivity() adds small Gaussian noise mediators outcome re-runs mediation. conclusions change tiny perturbations, fragile begin . Compare means unperturbed ones : close.
code: sensitivity <- bridge_sensitivity(   data            = data,   treatment       = "treatment",   mediators       = c("mediator_1", "mediator_2"),   outcome         = "outcome",   n_bootstraps    = 25,   perturbation_sd = 0.1,   parallel        = FALSE,   seed            = 42 )  round(sapply(sensitivity$perturbed_results$summaries, `[[`, "mean"), 3) #>  direct_effect   total_effect nie_mediator_1 nie_mediator_2  #>          2.515          5.982          2.259          1.208

title: Getting started with BriDGE
text: bridge_analyze() runs whole pipeline — discovery, mediation, group comparison, sensitivity, plots, text summary: result object keeps every component: results$discovery, results$mediation, results$comparison, results$plots.

CAUSAL DISCOVERY: #>    Method: mmhc #>    DAG Agreement: 80% #>  #> 2. MEDIATION ANALYSIS: #>    direct_effect: 2.4909 (95% CI: 2.2884 to 2.7229) #>    total_effect: 6.0235 (95% CI: 5.5377 to 6.5284) #>    nie_mediator_1: 2.2756 (95% CI: 1.8739 to 2.6741) #>    nie_mediator_2: 1.257 (95% CI: 0.9222 to 1.5909) #>  #> 3. COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS: #>    mediator_1 - Difference: 0.9863 #>    mediator_2 - Difference: 0.8619 #>    outcome - Difference: 5.6716 #>  #> ==== END SUMMARY ==== results$plots$effect_sizes results$plots$bootstrap_distributions

title: Getting started with BriDGE
text: Sample size: mediation estimands need power average treatment effects; aim hundreds observations, treat discovery output small samples exploratory. Bootstraps: 500 minimum stable percentile intervals; publication. Convergence: small bootstrap samples GAMs occasionally struggle. handle_convergence = "simplify" automatically falls back simpler models; "error" makes failures loud instead. Reproducibility: pass seed = make bootstrap draws reproducible, report . simpler tools suffice: one mediator, interaction nonlinearity suspected, classic linear mediation may need — see decision flowchart companion paper (Figure 1).

title: BriDGE 1.1.0
text: New “Getting started BriDGE” vignette walking full workflow: data requirements, causal discovery read DAG comparison, GAM-based mediation effect interpretation, sensitivity analysis, practical guidance (vignette("BriDGE")). New package website built pkgdown: https://gav888.github.io/BriDGE/. Added CITATION.cff GitHub shows “Cite repository” button. Added CONTRIBUTING.md issue templates (bug report, feature request). README now shows researcher-vs-discovered DAG comparison figure. Added test-coverage pkgdown CI workflows.

title: BriDGE 1.0.0
text: First public release, accompanying accepted paper: Veltri, G. ., & Banerjee, S. (press). BriDGE gap – improving Behavioural research integrating DAGs GAMs Experiments. Behavior Research Methods.

title: BriDGE 1.0.0
text: package title description now use paper’s expansion acronym: Behavioural research integrating DAGs GAMs Experiments. bridge_mediate() bridge_compare() now require treatment variable exactly two levels raise informative error otherwise.

title: BriDGE 1.0.0
text: bridge_mediate() bridge_compare() longer hardcode treatment levels "0"/"1". two-level coding (e.g. "control"/"treatment") now works; first factor level taken control, second treated.

title: BriDGE 1.0.0
text: New seed argument bridge_analyze(), bridge_mediate(), bridge_sensitivity() reproducible bootstrap resampling perturbation (previously fixed internal seed used). New summary() method bridge_analysis objects. companion simulation scripts reproduce paper’s results now shipped inst/simulations/ (see system.file("simulations", package = "BriDGE")). Added citation information (citation("BriDGE")).

title: BriDGE 1.0.0
text: Package moved repository root, devtools::install_github("gav888/BriDGE") works directly. Unit tests moved tests/testthat/ run R CMD check; added regression tests treatment coding, seeding, new summary() method. License formalized MIT + file LICENSE; repository URL corrected. Added GitHub Actions R-CMD-check workflow.
